passages.title: Email: training session moved
passages.body:
To: All sales staff
From: Marcus Bell, Training Coordinator
Subject: Product training rescheduled

Due to a scheduling conflict at the conference center, the product training that (1) ___ for Tuesday has been moved to Thursday, May 9. The session will still begin at 9:00 A.M. in Room 4. (2) ___. Attendees should bring their laptops, as the afternoon workshop requires them. (3) ___ you cannot attend on the new date, please notify me by Friday so that I can arrange a recorded version. Thank you for your (4) ___.

passages.title: Notice: building maintenance
passages.body:
NOTICE TO TENANTS

The building's elevators (1) ___ for inspection on Saturday, June 15, between 8:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M. During that time, tenants are asked to use the stairs. (2) ___. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. The inspection is part of our (3) ___ effort to keep the building safe. Residents with mobility difficulties may call the front desk, and a staff member will (4) ___ them with their luggage or groceries.

passages.title: Article: city bike-sharing program
passages.body:
CITY LAUNCHES BIKE-SHARING PROGRAM

SPRINGFIELD (March 3) — City officials announced yesterday that a bike-sharing program will begin next month, with 40 stations located (1) ___ the downtown area. Residents will be able to rent a bicycle for a flat fee of two dollars per hour. (2) ___. Mayor Julia Park said the program is intended to reduce traffic and (3) ___ healthier habits. Although similar programs have succeeded elsewhere, (4) ___ officials caution that the city's hills could limit its popularity.

passages.title: Memo: remote work policy
passages.body:
MEMO

To: All employees
From: Human Resources
Date: October 2
Re: Updated remote work policy

Beginning November 1, employees (1) ___ work from home up to two days per week, provided that their supervisor approves. (2) ___. Remote employees must be available during core hours, from 10:00 A.M. to 3:00 P.M. Equipment such as monitors and chairs may be borrowed, but (3) ___ items must be returned if the arrangement ends. We believe this policy will improve both productivity and (4) ___ satisfaction.

passages.title: Letter: job offer
passages.body:
Dear Ms. Ortega,

It gives me great pleasure to offer you the position of Senior Accountant at Harlow & Finch, (1) ___ on June 3. Your annual salary will be $68,000, and you will be eligible for health insurance after ninety days. (2) ___. Please sign and return the enclosed contract by May 20. (3) ___ you have any questions, do not hesitate to contact me. We are (4) ___ to welcoming you to our team.

passages.title: Advertisement: language courses
passages.body:
BRIDGE LANGUAGE ACADEMY

Improve your career prospects with a language course at Bridge Academy! Our instructors are native speakers (1) ___ more than ten years of teaching experience. Classes are offered in the morning, afternoon and evening. (2) ___. Register by August 31 and you will (3) ___ a 15 percent discount on your first term. Spaces are limited, so (4) ___ early to avoid disappointment.

passages.title: Email: apology for shipment delay
passages.body:
To: Mr. Yuen
From: Customer Care, Redwood Furniture
Subject: Your order #44721

Dear Mr. Yuen,

We are sorry to inform you that your dining table (1) ___ on May 12 as promised. A shortage of oak panels at our supplier caused the delay. (2) ___. The new delivery date is May 20, and the shipping fee will be refunded to your card. (3) ___ we cannot change the delay, we hope this gesture shows how much we value your (4) ___.

passages.title: Announcement: museum exhibit
passages.body:
HARTWELL MUSEUM — NEW EXHIBIT

This fall, the Hartwell Museum (1) ___ a major exhibit on the history of navigation, featuring more than 200 historic instruments. (2) ___. Guided tours run daily at 11:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., and (3) ___ tickets can be purchased online at a reduced price. Members enjoy free admission. We invite you to (4) ___ this fascinating journey through time.

fr.rule: Passif au prétérit : la formation « était programmée ».
why_wrong: A : actif : la formation ne programme pas elle-même.
D : actif présent : le sujet ne programme pas.
A: active: the training does not schedule itself.
D: active present: the subject does not schedule.

choices: The agenda and the list of speakers remain unchanged.
Parking is expensive near the airport.
The conference center will close in June.

fr.rule: La phrase prolonge le changement de date en rassurant sur le programme.
why_wrong: D : information sans rapport avec la formation.
fr.example: The agenda and the list of speakers remain unchanged.

en.rule: The sentence extends the date change by reassuring about the program.
en.example: The agenda and the list of speakers remain unchanged.

fr.rule: If + présent = condition réelle.
why_wrong: A : « unless » inverse le sens : « à moins que vous ne puissiez pas… ».

fr.rule: Après un possessif : nom (understanding).
why_wrong: C : verbe : un nom/gérondif est attendu après « your ».
D : adjectif : il manque le nom.
C: verb: a noun/gerund is expected after 'your'.
D: adjective: the noun is missing.

fr.rule: Futur passif : « will be shut down ».
why_wrong: A : passé : la date est dans le futur.
B : actif présent : le sujet ne ferme pas lui-même.
D : participe sans auxiliaire : phrase incomplète.
A: past: the date is in the future.
B: active present: the subject does not shut itself.
D: participle with no auxiliary: incomplete sentence.

choices: Rents will rise by five percent next year.
Notices will also be posted in each lobby.

fr.rule: La phrase ajoute une précision sur l'information donnée aux locataires.
why_wrong: A : information historique sans lien avec la phrase suivante.
fr.example: Notices will also be posted in each lobby.

en.rule: The sentence adds a detail about informing tenants.
why_wrong: A: historical detail unrelated to the next sentence.
en.example: Notices will also be posted in each lobby.

fr.rule: ongoing = en cours, continu (adjectif).
why_wrong: C : adverbe : un adjectif est attendu devant « effort ».
C: adverb: an adjective is expected before 'effort'.

fr.rule: assist someone with something = aider.
throughout = partout dans.
why_wrong: A : « since » s'emploie pour le temps.
C : « during » s'emploie pour une durée.
D : « between » demande deux éléments précis.

choices: Many residents prefer to take the bus.
Payment can be made with a card or through a smartphone app.

fr.rule: La phrase suit logiquement le tarif en précisant le paiement.
why_wrong: A : information sans lien avec le tarif.
B : contredit l'idée de promotion du programme.
fr.example: Payment can be made with a card or through a smartphone app.

en.rule: The sentence follows the fee by explaining payment.
why_wrong: A: information unrelated to the fee.
en.example: Payment can be made with a card or through a smartphone app.

fr.rule: encourage = encourager (cohérent avec « healthier habits »).
some officials = certains responsables.
why_wrong: C : « any » s'emploie surtout dans les phrases négatives et interrogatives.
C: 'any' is used mostly in negatives and questions.

fr.rule: may = permission.
why_wrong: A : conditionnel : ne convient pas à une règle.
D : obligation : sens incorrect pour une permission.
A: conditional: does not suit a rule.
D: obligation: wrong meaning for a permission.

choices: The company was founded by two engineers.
Requests should be submitted at least one week in advance.
Several employees have moved to other cities.
The cafeteria is closed on Mondays.

fr.rule: La phrase précise la procédure d'approbation.
fr.example: Requests should be submitted at least one week in advance.

en.rule: The sentence specifies the approval procedure.
en.example: Requests should be submitted at least one week in advance.

fr.rule: these items = ces objets.
why_wrong: C : pronom : il faut un déterminant devant « items ».
C: pronoun: a determiner is needed before 'items'.

fr.rule: employee satisfaction = satisfaction des employés (nom composé).
why_wrong: C : participe/adjectif : un nom est attendu.
C: participle/adjective: a noun is expected.

fr.rule: Participe présent pour une précision de date : « starting on June 3 ».
why_wrong: A : présent : la phrase deviendrait deux propositions sans liaison.
B : base verbale : incorrect après la virgule.
D : participe passé : sens passif incorrect.

en.rule: Present participle for a date detail: 'starting on June 3'.
why_wrong: A: present: this would make two clauses with no link.
B: base form: incorrect after the comma.
D: past participle: passive sense wrong.

choices: The office has recently been repainted.
You will also receive twenty days of paid vacation per year.
Ms. Ortega's previous employer was located in Madrid.

fr.rule: La phrase continue la liste des avantages.
fr.example: You will also receive twenty days of paid vacation per year.

en.rule: The sentence continues the list of benefits.
en.example: You will also receive twenty days of paid vacation per year.

fr.rule: Should you have… = If you have… (formel).
why_wrong: B : ne forme pas l'inversion conditionnelle.

en.rule: Should you have… = If you have… (formal).
why_wrong: B: does not form the conditional inversion.

fr.rule: look forward to + -ing.
with + possession : avec plus de dix ans d'expérience.
why_wrong: B : « at » ne s'emploie pas ici.
C : « by » exprime l'agent ou l'échéance.

en.rule: with + possession: with more than ten years' experience.

choices: Students may also choose between small groups and private lessons.
The academy opened in a former factory.

fr.rule: La phrase continue la présentation des modalités de cours.
fr.example: Students may also choose between small groups and private lessons.

en.rule: The sentence continues describing course formats.
en.example: Students may also choose between small groups and private lessons.

fr.rule: will + base verbale.
why_wrong: D : présent parfait : sens futur attendu.
D: present perfect: future meaning expected.

fr.rule: Impératif : register early.

why_wrong: C: gerund: an imperative is expected.

fr.rule: Passif modal passé : « could not be delivered ».
why_wrong: B : actif et futur : sens incorrect.
C : actif : la table ne livre pas.

en.rule: Past modal passive: 'could not be delivered'.
why_wrong: B: active and future: wrong meaning.
C: active: the table does not deliver.

choices: Oak is a common wood in the region.
Our showroom has recently been renovated.
Your order is now scheduled for the next available truck.

fr.rule: La phrase annonce la solution, introduite avant la nouvelle date.
why_wrong: C : sans lien avec la livraison.
fr.example: Your order is now scheduled for the next available truck.

en.rule: The sentence announces the solution before the new date.
en.example: Your order is now scheduled for the next available truck.

fr.rule: Although + proposition = bien que.
your patience = votre patience (nom).
why_wrong: C : adjectif : un nom est attendu après « your ».
A: = people receiving treatment: different meaning.
C: adjective: a noun is expected after 'your'.

fr.rule: Présent continu à valeur de programme.
why_wrong: B : prétérit : « this fall » annonce un événement à venir ou en cours.
B: past: 'this fall' announces a current/upcoming event.

choices: The museum café serves excellent coffee.
The museum is closed on Mondays.
Parking is available behind the building.
Many of the items have never been displayed in public before.

fr.rule: La phrase prolonge la description de l'exposition.
why_wrong: B : hors sujet à ce stade.
C : pratique mais sans lien avec le contenu de l'exposition.
fr.example: Many of the items have never been displayed in public before.

en.rule: The sentence extends the exhibit's description.
why_wrong: B: off topic at this point.
C: practical but unrelated to the exhibit's content.
en.example: Many of the items have never been displayed in public before.

fr.rule: advance tickets = billets à l'avance.
why_wrong: D : nom : « advancement tickets » est incorrect.

fr.rule: embark on a journey = se lancer dans un voyage.

en.rule: embark on a journey = begin a journey.
